nodes.description: The meiotic block depletes germ cells in both sexes, producing ovarian follicle depletion with primary ovarian insufficiency in 46,XX individuals and germ-cell-depleted testes with non-obstructive azoospermia in 46,XY individuals. evidence.snippet: Our study identified novel pathogenic variations of C14ORF39 and SYCE1 in sporadic patients with POI or NOA, highlighting the essential role of SC genes in the maintenance of ovarian and testicular function.

nodes.description: SYCE1 forms the central element of the synaptonemal complex and is required for physical synapsis of homologous chromosomes during meiotic prophase I. Its loss prevents stable synapsis of homologous chromosome pairs, leaving them unsynapsed at the pachytene stage.

nodes.description: Unsynapsed chromosomes or persistent recombination intermediates from failed synapsis activate the meiotic pachytene checkpoint, which surveys for completion of synapsis and crossover formation. Checkpoint activation arrests germ cells at the pachytene stage of prophase I; persistently arrested cells are eliminated by apoptosis, depleting the germ-cell pool.

evidence.reference_title: Novel copy number variations within SYCE1 caused meiotic arrest and non-obstructive azoospermia.
evidence.snippet: H&E and IF staining demonstrated that the spermatogenesis was arrested at pachytene stage in the two patients with NOA, suggesting these two novel CNVs within SYCE1 could lead to meiotic defect and NOA.

nodes.description: Although microsurgical testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE) is the standard surgical sperm-retrieval intervention offered in idiopathic non-obstructive azoospermia, combined multicenter and literature data show uniformly negative sperm retrieval (0/14) in men carrying pathogenic or likely pathogenic SYCE1 variants due to complete pachytene-stage meiotic arrest; pre-TESE genetic diagnosis therefore enables patients to be informed that the likelihood of retrieving spermatozoa is virtually zero and helps avoid futile invasive surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Testicular sperm extraction: microdissection improves sperm yield with minimal tissue excision.
evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that microdissection TESE can improve sperm retrieval for men with non-obstructive azoospermia over that achieved with previously described biopsy techniques.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic determinants of testicular sperm extraction outcomes: insights from a large multicentre study of men with non-obstructive azoospermia.
evidence.snippet: Variants in 19 genes were consistently linked to negative TESE outcomes, with genes such as MSH4, SYCE1, and TEX11 mutated in a relatively large number of patients. Therefore, patients carrying LP/P variants in these genes should be informed that the likelihood of obtaining spermatozoa by TESE is virtually zero.

nodes.description: SYCE1 encodes a central element protein of the synaptonemal complex (SC). Biallelic loss-of-function abolishes SYCE1 protein and disrupts its interactions with the transverse-filament protein SYCP1 and the central element partner SIX6OS1/C14ORF39, so the SC central element cannot assemble and homologous chromosomes fail to synapse during meiotic prophase I.
